source_text:
Fragmentum in epistulam ii ad Thessalonicenses
2 Thess 2,78 Ὅταν μέντοι τὸ πέρας ἐπιστῇ τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ προθεσμίας, καὶ ὁ
νῦν κατέχων αὐτὸν ὅρος ἐκστῇ πληρωθείς, ἑτοίμως τότε καὶ δίχα πάσης ἀναβολῆς ὁ
ἄνομος ἀποκαλυφθήσεται.
thought_title: The appointed time and the removal of the boundary
orientation: Gennadius is commenting on 2 Thessalonians 2:7-8, explaining when and how the lawless one will be revealed.
pass_a_gloss: Fragment on the Second Epistle to the Thessalonians. 2 Thess 2,78. But when the end of God's appointed time arrives, and the boundary that now restrains him steps aside, its purpose fulfilled, then immediately and without any delay the lawless one will be revealed.

choices.english: the boundary that now restrains him
choices.why: The glossary specifies 'boundary' for ὅρος and 'what now restrains' for ὁ κατέχων; rendering the participle as a relative clause keeps the present restraining force clear while preserving the noun boundary as the subject.
rejected: the boundary now holding him back

choices.why: The aorist passive participle πληρωθείς indicates the boundary's fulfillment is completed before it steps aside; keeping the participle as a separate clause preserves the causal-temporal nuance.

choices.term: ἑτοίμως τότε καὶ δίχα πάσης ἀναβολῆς
choices.english: then readily and without any delay
choices.why: ἑτοίμως means 'readily' or 'promptly,' and δίχα πάσης ἀναβολῆς is emphatic ('without any delay at all'); rendering both adverbs keeps the double emphasis on immediacy.
rejected: at once and with no postponement

choices.why: The glossary mandates 'the lawless one' and bans alternatives like 'the man of lawlessness' or 'the wicked one.'

pass_b_english: Gennadius writes: But when the end of God's appointed time arrives, and the boundary that now restrains the lawless one is removed, its purpose fulfilled, then the lawless one will be revealed promptly and without any delay.
notes: The source notation '2 Thess 2,78' appears to be a typographical error or unusual notation, likely intended as 2:7-8 or 2:7,8.

problems.quote: promptly and without any delay
problems.why: Same Greek word rendered two ways; reader may think distinction intended.
problems.fix: Choose one translation consistently.

problems.quote: has been fulfilled and steps aside
problems.why: Same clause with reversed word order; reader may think different events.
problems.fix: Standardize word order across variants.

variants.text: has been fulfilled and steps aside

problems.quote: the lawless one
problems.why: No indication this is Paul's term from 2 Thessalonians 2:8; reader may think author's own term.
problems.fix: Identify as Paul's phrase or Scripture quotation.

problems.quote: the boundary that now restrains him has been fulfilled
problems.why: Boundary cannot be 'fulfilled'; abstract entity lacks goal to complete.
problems.fix: Translate 'when his task is complete' or similar.

problems.quote: boundary
problems.why: 'Boundary' is wrong for katechon; restrainer is person/force, not limit.
problems.fix: Use 'restrainer' or 'one who restrains.'

problems.quote: promptly
problems.why: Greek means 'in his own time' or 'at once,' not 'quickly after delay.'
problems.fix: Use 'then' or 'at that moment.'

problems.quote: the boundary that now restrains him has been fulfilled and steps aside
problems.why: Same concept, different clause order across variants; reader may wonder if meaning differs.
problems.fix: Standardize clause order or note these are manuscript variants.

variants.text: has been fulfilled and steps aside

problems.quote: revealed promptly and without any delay
problems.why: 'Promptly' vs 'readily' for same Greek word; reader may see a nuance difference where none exists.
problems.fix: Use one adverb consistently across all variants.

The mistranslation problem about 'promptly' is fixed by using 'at once'.

The adverb 'immediately' is used consistently in the English and matches the glossary entry for 'ἑτοίμως'.

polish.changed: Clarified that the boundary restrains 'the lawless one' rather than an ambiguous 'him,' and adjusted the verb from 'steps aside' to 'is removed' to avoid a mixed metaphor with an inanimate boundary.

notes.quote: the boundary that now restrains him
notes.why: Never explains what 'boundary' means; biblical scholarship debates this (Roman Empire? Holy Spirit? Angel?)
notes.fix: Add footnote: 'Greek to katechon, the restrainer'.

notes.why: No explanation that this means the Antichrist; assumes reader knows eschatological terminology.
notes.fix: Add 'i.e., the Antichrist' in first occurrence.

notes.why: Four sections show same words with phrase moved; reader cannot tell if author, scribe, or editor speaks.

notes.quote: the boundary that now restrains him steps aside, its purpose fulfilled
notes.why: Inanimate 'boundary' cannot 'step aside'; mixed metaphor with animate verb.
'Boundary' suggests a limit or border; context requires something active that restrains a person.
Implies voluntary action by person; if 'boundary' is abstract (Roman Empire?), 'steps aside' is odd.
A first-time reader may not know this refers to the Antichrist figure from 2 Thessalonians 2.
notes.fix: Add a brief note identifying the lawless one as the Antichrist.

notes.quote: the boundary that now restrains him
notes.why: The restraining boundary is a technical concept from 2 Thess 2:6-7 never explained here.
notes.fix: Add a note explaining the 'boundary' as the restraining power of 2 Thess 2.
